summary: The merge is semantically correct. I checked it against both parents: master 020566aa (md5 82c368f4 matches) plus only the norm-gather hunks; bd60e2db plus only the fa3c hunks; it py_compiles. The interaction it tests (fixed ~146/29/10 us norm+gather saving, additive across the attention boundary) is plausible, and the profile and PATH CHOSEN lines can read it even though the ~0.9% headline gain sits inside the +-1.5% CI.
justification: A. MERGE VERIFIED, not just textually. diff(master, merged) has exactly six hunks, all from norm-gather. (1) `import inspect`. (2) state['pre_expert_w'] = weights['pre_expert_norm'] in bf16, a weight and not input-derived. (3) prepare order is _ssdq_setup -> _rega_setup -> fa3c_lines = _fa3c_setup(...) -> _norm_gather_setup(state, device, t_prepare0) -> sync, then align2_lines and fa3c_lines are printed again. So both new setups run after _rega_setup, norm-gather comes after fa3c, and fa3c_lines is still printed. (4) _experts(pre_norm=False) applies the module norm on every non-fused branch: rega OFF, ssdq, marlin, triton, and rega ON with norm_gather OFF. Every path except the fused one is therefore byte-identical to master's behaviour. (5) _experts_rega(prenorm=) swaps rega_gather for _norm_gather only when prenorm is set. (6) The NG_* block and kernel_fn's call changes to _experts(expert_input, ..., pre_norm=True). diff(bd60e2db source, merged) has four hunks: the two fa3c prepare lines, the _fa3c_* block and the FA3 call site. All _REGA_*, _rega_setup, align2 and _fa3c_* strings are untouched. Deadlines: FA3C_START_DEADLINE_S 235, FA3C_CLASS_DEADLINE_S 265, NG_BUDGET_S 270, REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S 150 and REGA_COPY_DEADLINE_S 255, all unchanged. The prepare estimate is ~125.5 s of 300 s. The rega gating dispatch at line ~3783 calls _experts without pre_norm, so rega's own gates still time master's normed input. Mechanism: the fused kernel reads raw rows once and writes the normed sorted slots, removing one full [T, 4096] bf16 write+read and a launch. The edf68fa3 gate measured cold-L2 graph medians of pair 216.9/42.8/14.8 us against fused 71.0/14.0/5.2 us. Against the FINDINGS rows (sliding ft 10947, turn_4 2153, turn_1 720 us) that is ~1.3% on sliding and ~0.8-1.2% on full, which matches `expected`, all directions faster. WEAKEST LINK: the headline. A weighted ~0.9% gain is well inside the CI half-width (~+-1.5%) and inside the stated +-3-4% per-row noise. So the score cannot confirm additivity, and the sliding-ft 'remaining 3% was drift' claim cannot be checked from rows either. Both can only be read from the profile: _norm_gather_kernel ~71/14/5 us replacing the pre_expert_norm + rega_gather rows, and the FA3 rows on full first_turn unchanged against master's job 1cc92a43. A second weak point is that the gate timings are cold-L2 isolated graphs. In-layer, the pair's norm output may partly hit L2 (pooler output 16384x4096 bf16 = 128 MiB at ft, so not at ft; but 6/24 MiB at turn_1/turn_4 does fit the 50 MB L2). The real turn_1/turn_4 saving may therefore be smaller than the gate ratio implies.
confounders: fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated (020566aa, master): the only source never co-run with norm-gather. It writes contiguous K/V buffers (persistent in state['fa3c']['route']) before FA3 on full layers. Norm-gather runs after o-proj, boundary and pooler on the same stream with no shared buffers. An L2 or allocator interaction is possible in principle but unlikely; only full-layer rows could show it, and sliding rows act as the internal control.

experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 / experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128: norm-gather exists only where rega_ok[class] is ON, and replaces rega_gather's input. If a rega gate flips OFF in this run (prepare noise near the 0.95 ft ratio is not a concern at 0.554), norm-gather silently becomes a no-op for that class. Read the [rega] PATH CHOSEN lines before attributing any row.

align-two-phase-all-t-rega: produces the sorted_ids/block_experts/n_padded that the fused kernel consumes. The norm-gather self-check runs _align_dispatch on the live state, so it is already validated against align2. No confound to the timing beyond the shared base.

sglang-pipeline-parity: defines state['pre_expert_norm'] (the module whose effective weight is bf16, hence round_w=True). The fused path's numerics are checked against it within 1 ulp; there is no timing confound.
interference: No companion. Checks are spent and this is a scored submit, so any companion would also cost a scored run. None would make the result less ambiguous than the run's own logs already do. The interaction under test (norm-gather saving vs contiguous-KV FA3) is separated inside this single run: sliding layers are untouched by fa3c and carry norm-gather alone, while full layers carry both. The kernel-level readout (profile rows _norm_gather_kernel vs master's pre_expert_norm + rega_gather, and the FA3 rows vs 1cc92a43) attributes each side directly. An ab-revert of fa3c would just reproduce edf68fa3 (already scored, 1.4600), and an ab-revert of norm-gather is master (1cc92a43, 1.4587). Both arms of the 2x2 already exist on the board, so this run completes the factorial. Combination B also uses this run as its paired control. Judge it on: [norm-gather] PATH CHOSEN = fused in all three classes, the [fa3 contig] PATH CHOSEN line equal to master's (B at the three full first_turn shapes), profile rows as above, and no first_turn row slower than master by more than noise. A headline within CI of 1.4587-1.4600 is the expected outcome and is not a refutation.
rules_flags: None blocking. kernel_fn dispatches only on the token count (a shape) and prepare-set bools. The fused kernel recomputes RMSNorm from the raw input on every call (no input-derived caching). pre_expert_w is a checkpoint weight. n_padded is read on-device, so there is no host sync. grid = min(nprog, sorted_ids.numel()) uses a shape, not a value.

Minor: Triton JIT specialization. num_routes and nprog are do_not_specialize, but pointer-alignment specialization of x/xs could in principle differ between the prepare-time test tensors and kernel_fn's tensors and trigger a compile inside the timed call. This was not seen in edf68fa3 (same code, passed the judge), and in this merge kernel_fn's inputs are produced by the same _gemm path, so the risk is low.

Precision: round_w=True was chosen by the self-check (1 + w rounded to bf16, matching the module's bf16 effective weight). fp32 math with one bf16 rounding; whole-expert-output and two-state replay rel L2 <= 1e-3, both gated in prepare.
open_questions: '[norm-gather] setup took 0.7s' in edf68fa3 looks low for three classes of self-checks plus 21-alternation cold-L2 timing (maybe Triton cache hits or a timer quirk). It is harmless under the 270 s budget, but confirm the per-class GATE lines print in full again here.
At turn_1/turn_4 the pooler output (6/24 MiB) fits in L2, so the in-layer pair cost may be below the cold-L2 gate's 14.8/42.8 us. Does the profile show the expected ~10/29 us saving, or less?

If the full first_turn FA3 rows differ from 1cc92a43 beyond noise while the [fa3 contig] PATH CHOSEN line is identical, that is the L2/allocator interaction the conjecture names. It would need a follow-up, not a revert.
